creativeFence.title: Creative Autopilot
creativeFence.intro: The one campaign and ad set where the creative engine may switch its own ads on and off. It must contain that ad set and nothing else, and the ad set needs a daily budget at or below the cap below. The engine verifies this every sweep and refuses to act if anything does not match — it can never change a budget.

breach.body: Everything inside Autopilot was paused. Activations stay blocked until you resume.

creativeLifecycle.title: Creative Lifecycle Rules
creativeLifecycle.intro: How the engine judges a live ad. Clicks kill and purchases crown — never the other way round, because a large share of perfectly healthy ads show zero purchases. Leave a field blank to use the value shown beside it.

graceMinAgeDays.label: Grace period (days)
graceMinAgeDays.hint: No verdict before an ad is this old.

minImpressions.label: Minimum impressions
minImpressions.hint: No verdict below this much evidence.

killMarginRatio.label: Kill margin
killMarginRatio.hint: How far below normal a click rate must credibly sit at the minimum sample.

killMarginRatioMax.label: Kill margin (max evidence)
killMarginRatioMax.hint: The margin relaxes toward this as evidence accumulates.

crownMinAgeDays.label: Crown age (days)
crownMinAgeDays.hint: Crowning requires a longer life than grace.

crownMinPurchases.label: Crown minimum purchases
crownMinPurchases.hint: Purchases only ever crown — they never kill.

crownMinPeers.label: Crown minimum peers
crownMinPeers.hint: Live peers needed before “above median” means anything.

toast.savedDescription: The engine uses these on its next nightly sweep.

dailyDigest.title: Daily Digest
dailyDigest.intro: Each morning Adcero reviews yesterday's ad performance against the prior 7-day baseline and posts a concise, read-only digest — headline, key findings, and recommended next actions — to your Ask Adcero chat and dashboard. Turn on email below to also receive it in your inbox. Digests pause automatically for accounts no one has opened in over a week, and resume on your next visit.

meta.label: Meta (Facebook/Instagram)

meta.tooltip: List, create, update, delete, and duplicate Meta campaigns, ad sets, and ads. Search interests, locations, and languages for targeting. Manage automated rules and estimate audience size.

metaRead.description: Read Meta campaigns, ad accounts, targeting, pages, pixels, and datasets
metaRead.tooltip: Read Meta campaigns, ad accounts, pages, Instagram accounts, pixels, datasets, and targeting options. No write access — cannot create or modify campaigns.

metaWrite.label: Meta (Write)
metaWrite.description: Create and manage Meta campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, and rules
metaWrite.tooltip: Create, update, delete, and duplicate Meta campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, and automated rules. Includes media upload and A/B experiment management.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.description: Campaigns, ad groups, ads, and targeting on TikTok
tiktok.tooltip: List, create, update, and manage TikTok campaigns, ad groups, and ads. Browse interest and action categories, locations, languages, audiences, and carriers for targeting.

tiktokRead.label: TikTok (Read-Only)
tiktokRead.description: Browse TikTok targeting options and identity profiles
tiktokRead.tooltip: Browse TikTok interest/action categories, locations, languages, audiences, carriers, and identity profiles. Read-only — cannot create or modify campaigns.

tiktokWrite.label: TikTok (Write)
tiktokWrite.description: Create and manage TikTok campaigns, ad groups, ads, and media
tiktokWrite.tooltip: Create and manage TikTok campaigns, ad groups, ads, and media uploads.

googleAds.label: Google Ads
googleAds.description: Campaigns, ad groups, ads, targeting, and assets on Google Ads
googleAds.tooltip: List, create, update, and delete Google Ads campaigns, ad groups, and ads. Search locations, languages, audiences, topics, and keywords for targeting. Manage assets, conversion actions, and Merchant Center accounts.

googleAdsRead.label: Google Ads (Read-Only)
googleAdsRead.description: Read Google Ads campaigns, accounts, targeting, and conversion data
googleAdsRead.tooltip: Read Google Ads campaigns, accounts, conversion actions, Merchant Center data, field options, targeting options, and app search results. No write access.

googleAdsWrite.label: Google Ads (Write)
googleAdsWrite.description: Create and manage Google Ads campaigns, ad groups, ads, and assets
googleAdsWrite.tooltip: Create, update, and delete Google Ads campaigns, ad groups, ads, and assets.

twitter.label: X (Twitter)
twitter.description: Campaigns, ad groups, ads, targeting, and media on X
twitter.tooltip: Read, create, and manage X (Twitter) campaigns, ad groups, and ads. Search targeting options, resolve identity accounts, and upload media.

twitterRead.label: X (Read-Only)
twitterRead.description: Read X campaigns, targeting options, and identity accounts
twitterRead.tooltip: Read X campaigns, search targeting options, and list the identity accounts ads can run as. No write access — cannot create or modify campaigns.

twitterWrite.label: X (Write)
twitterWrite.description: Create and manage X campaigns, ad groups, ads, and media
twitterWrite.tooltip: Create, update, and delete X campaigns, ad groups (line items), and ads. Includes media upload.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn
linkedin.description: Draft campaigns and ads, targeting lookups, and Page identities on LinkedIn
linkedin.tooltip: Create DRAFT LinkedIn campaigns, ad sets, and ads, upload ad media, and delete drafts. Look up targeting locations and the LinkedIn Pages ads can be authored as.

linkedinRead.label: LinkedIn (Read-Only)
linkedinRead.description: Look up LinkedIn locations and the Pages you can advertise as
linkedinRead.tooltip: Look up LinkedIn targeting locations and the Pages ads can be authored as. Read-only — cannot create or modify campaigns. Campaign performance is read through Cross-Platform.

linkedinWrite.label: LinkedIn (Write)
linkedinWrite.description: Create draft LinkedIn campaigns, ad sets, and ads, and upload media
linkedinWrite.tooltip: Create DRAFT LinkedIn campaigns, ad sets, and ads, upload ad media, and delete drafts. Activation happens in LinkedIn Campaign Manager.

pinterest.label: Pinterest
pinterest.description: Pinterest lookups and paused campaign creation
pinterest.tooltip: Look up Pinterest targeting, keywords, boards and Pins, audiences, and conversion readiness, and create PAUSED campaigns, ad groups, ads, and Pins. Activation happens in Pinterest Ads Manager.

pinterestRead.label: Pinterest (Read-Only)
pinterestRead.description: Look up Pinterest targeting, Pins, and audiences
pinterestRead.tooltip: Look up Pinterest targeting locations, interests, keyword search volume, boards and Pins, audience lists, conversion readiness, and the ad account currency. Read-only — cannot create or modify campaigns. Campaign performance is read through Cross-Platform.

pinterestWrite.label: Pinterest (Write)
pinterestWrite.description: Create paused Pinterest campaigns, ad groups, ads, and Pins
pinterestWrite.tooltip: Create PAUSED Pinterest campaigns, ad groups, and ads, add keywords, create ad-only boards and Pins, and archive campaigns, ad groups, and ads. Budget and bid changes and activation happen in Pinterest Ads Manager.

crossPlatform.label: Cross-Platform
crossPlatform.description: Ads Manager, dashboard, analytics, and attribution
crossPlatform.tooltip: Query the Ads Manager for cross-platform campaign data. Access dashboard KPIs, analytics charts, and attribution reports. Read campaign/ad set/ad records from the database.

attribution.label: Attribution
attribution.description: Commerce data, owned channels, surveys, and attribution engine
attribution.tooltip: Query commerce orders, refunds, and order events. Access email/SMS campaign engagement and revenue data. Manage post-purchase survey responses and channel mappings. Run attribution journeys, model comparisons, ad spend analysis, and conversion delivery monitoring.

assets.label: Assets & AI

assets.tooltip: Upload, organize, and manage creative assets (images, videos). Generate AI ad copy, run policy compliance checks, and create content variations.

assetsRead.label: Assets (Read-Only)
assetsRead.tooltip: Browse and view uploaded creative assets (images, videos). Read-only — cannot upload or generate new content.

assetsWrite.label: Assets & AI (Write)
assetsWrite.description: Generate AI ad copy and content variations
assetsWrite.tooltip: Generate AI ad copy, run policy compliance checks, and create content variations using AI.

organizationRead.tooltip: View organization profile, settings, and user preferences, plus connected integrations, their sync history, and webhook health. Read-only — cannot modify members or connect, sync, or disconnect integrations.

organizationWrite.label: Organization (Write)
organizationWrite.description: Manage members, integrations, and organization settings

connect.title: Connect Shopify Store
connect.descriptionReview: Confirm the credentials captured by the browser automation
connect.descriptionPublic: Connect your Shopify store to Adcero
connect.descriptionCustom: Create a custom app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard to get started
connect.publicIntro: Enter your Shopify store domain and click Connect to authorize Adcero.
connect.domainHelp: Find this in your Shopify admin under Settings > Domains. Use the .myshopify.com domain.
connect.setupIntro: Follow these steps to create a custom app for your Shopify store:

devDashboard.title: Open the Dev Dashboard
devDashboard.body: Go to dev.shopify.com and open Apps. (From your Shopify admin: Settings > Apps → "Develop apps" → "Build apps in Dev Dashboard".)

createApp.title: Create the app manually
createApp.body: Click "Create app" and choose "Create app manually" from the menu — not the Shopify CLI option marked Recommended. Name the app "Adcero" (or any name you prefer).

scopes.title: Paste the scopes, then create and release
scopes.body: In the API access section, paste these scopes into the Scopes field:
scopes.historyNote: Leave read_all_orders out for now — Shopify refuses to create an app with it ("Contains invalid scopes"). Step 5 adds it later.
scopes.create: Click "Create app". Shopify immediately opens a Release version dialog — click "Release". Releasing is part of creating the app, not a separate later step.

protectedData.title: Approve protected customer data access
protectedData.intro: Look next to the scopes field — what you see depends on how the app was created:
protectedData.noLink: No "Request access" link? Apps created directly in the Dev Dashboard get protected customer data access automatically — there is nothing to request. Confirm read_orders is in the scopes from step 3 and continue.
protectedData.withLink: See "Some scopes require Shopify permission" with a "Request access" link? Click it — it opens the Partner Dashboard API access requests page. Under Protected customer data access, click "Request access", then:
protectedData.analytics: Check Analytics as the data-use reason, then click Save.
protectedData.fields: Under Protected customer fields, select Email and Phone (used to match orders to ad clicks).
protectedData.details: Under Data protection details, answer Yes to each question and Not applicable to the automated decision-making question, then Save.
protectedData.noReview: There is no Shopify review wait for custom apps. If the link is shown and skipped, order history imports stay blocked even after the app is installed.

fullHistory.title: Optional: Unlock full order history
fullHistory.body: Without read_all_orders, Shopify only shares the last 60 days of orders. Shopify unlocks it only after Custom distribution and an approved access request:
fullHistory.distribution: On the app Overview, click Distribution ("Select distribution method"). This opens the Partner Dashboard: choose Custom distribution, enter your store's .myshopify.com domain and click "Generate link". Ignore the install link it generates — you'll install from the Dev Dashboard in step 6.
fullHistory.partnerRequest: Still in the Partner Dashboard, open API access requests. Under Read all orders scope, click "Request access" and give the reason: "One-time historical order import to build the store's ad attribution baseline (ROAS and cost per acquisition against past campaigns). Ongoing orders arrive via webhooks." Access is granted immediately. This card appears for apps created in the Dev Dashboard too.
fullHistory.newVersion: Back in the Dev Dashboard, open Versions → "Create version", add read_all_orders to the end of the Scopes field, then click "Release".
fullHistory.rejected: If Shopify rejects the version with an error naming read_all_orders, the request isn't granted yet — remove read_all_orders, release with the rest, and try again once access is granted. The store still connects (60-day history plus live webhooks) in the meantime.

install.title: Install the app on your store
install.body: On the app Overview, click "Install app", choose your store, then click "Install".

credentials.title: Copy your credentials
credentials.body: Stay on the app Overview page. In the Credentials panel, you'll find:

howItWorks.title: How this works
howItWorks.body: Adcero tracks visitors and sales on your website by adding a small piece of code to it. Follow the 3 steps below — no coding experience needed. If you have a web developer, you can forward this page to them.

step1.title: Step 1 — Add the tracking code to your website
step1.intro: Click Copy below, then paste the code into your website so it appears on every page. Where to paste it:
step1.shopify: Shopify: Online Store → Themes → Edit code → theme.liquid → paste just before {closeHead}
step1.wordpress: WordPress: use a plugin like “Insert Headers and Footers” and paste into the Header section
step1.builders: Webflow / Squarespace / Wix: Site Settings → Custom Code → Head
step1.other: Other: paste inside the {openHead} section of every page

consent.title: Consent is required before anything is tracked
consent.body: Until consent is granted, the tracker sends nothing and stores no visitor ID. Once consent is granted, it records the current page view and the ad click IDs in its URL, and tracks from then on.
consent.banner: Have a consent banner? Call this when the visitor accepts analytics cookies, and {deny} when they decline:
consent.noBanner: No consent banner? Set the consent state before the Adcero script instead:
consent.legal: Only preset consent where you are allowed to track visitors without asking first. Check your privacy obligations (GDPR, ePrivacy, CCPA).

step2.title: Step 2 — Tell Adcero when a sale happens
step2.intro: So Adcero knows which ads led to real purchases, add this small snippet to your “Thank you” / order confirmation page (the page a customer sees after checkout). Replace the amount and email with your real order values.
step2.hint: Not sure where your confirmation page is? Most platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce, etc.) let you add scripts to the “Order Status” or “Thank you” page from their settings.

step3.title: Step 3 — Check that it’s working
step3.body: Visit your website in a new tab, then come back here and refresh this page. Once Adcero receives data, the status will change from {needsSetup} to {connected} and you’ll see an event counter appear.

advanced.title: Advanced — Server events API
advanced.body: Send purchases, refunds and leads from your server, authenticated with your API key. Optional: you don’t need this for the steps above.

disconnect.title: Disconnect Integration
disconnect.confirm: Are you sure you want to disconnect {name}?

consequence.default: This will stop tracking new events from this integration. Historical data will be preserved.
consequence.stripe: Adcero stops receiving payments from this Stripe account and deletes its access. Orders already imported stay in Adcero. To also remove the Adcero Attribution app from Stripe, uninstall it in Stripe → Settings → Installed apps.
consequence.recharge: Adcero stops receiving charges from this Recharge store and removes its webhooks there. Orders already imported stay in Adcero.
consequence.gumroad: Adcero stops receiving sales from this Gumroad account and removes its webhooks there. Sales already imported stay in Adcero. Gumroad keeps Adcero listed as an authorized app: to remove its access too, click Revoke access next to “Adcero Integration” in Gumroad → Settings → Applications.
consequence.shopify: Adcero stops receiving new orders from this store and removes its webhooks and automatically installed tracker from Shopify. Orders already imported stay in Adcero. Orders placed while the store is disconnected are not captured, even after you reconnect. A tracker snippet you pasted into your theme, or a checkout pixel you added in Customer events, keeps running until you remove it in Shopify.
consequence.shopifyHistoryImport: Adcero stops receiving new orders from this store and removes its webhooks and automatically installed tracker from Shopify. Orders already imported stay in Adcero. Orders placed while the store is disconnected are imported from Shopify’s order history when you reconnect, without live click attribution. A tracker snippet you pasted into your theme, or a checkout pixel you added in Customer events, keeps running until you remove it in Shopify.
consequence.woocommerce: Adcero removes its webhooks from this store and stops syncing orders; orders already imported stay in Adcero. The API key Adcero used stays active in WooCommerce — to remove access completely, revoke the key named "Adcero" (or "Adcero Attribution - API …") in WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API keys.
consequence.conversionLink: Adcero stops sending conversions through this connection. Ad accounts connected in Settings stay connected.
consequence.segment: Adcero stops accepting events from Segment. Events already received stay in Adcero. Also disable or delete the Webhooks (Actions) destination in Segment: it keeps sending events, and Adcero turns every one away.
consequence.klaviyo: This removes the Klaviyo connection in Adcero, and synced campaign metrics stop updating. Metrics already synced stay in Adcero. Also delete the Adcero webhook in Klaviyo (Settings → Webhooks): reconnecting creates a new webhook URL and signing secret.

crmConsequence.gohighlevel: Adcero stops receiving leads and deal updates from this sub-account and removes the Adcero Attribution app from it in GoHighLevel. Historical data is preserved.
crmConsequence.hubspot: Adcero stops receiving contacts and deal updates from this HubSpot account and uninstalls the Adcero app from it. Historical data is preserved.
crmConsequence.meta_lead_ads: Adcero stops receiving leads from these Facebook Pages. Leads already imported are preserved.

crmConsequence.linkedin_lead_gen: Adcero stops receiving Lead Gen Form responses from these LinkedIn ad accounts. Leads already imported are preserved.

firstTouch.name: First Click
firstTouch.description: 100% credit to the first click — measures which channel introduced the customer
firstTouch.difference: All credit goes to the first click in the journey. Favors top-of-funnel channels like awareness campaigns and discovery ads.

lastClick.name: Last Click
lastClick.description: 100% credit to the last touchpoint before conversion
lastClick.difference: All credit goes to the final touchpoint before conversion. Favors lower-funnel channels.

linear.name: Linear
linear.description: Equal credit distributed across all touchpoints
linear.difference: Distributes credit equally across all touchpoints. Upper-funnel channels (social discovery, awareness campaigns) receive more credit than under last-click.

timeDecay.name: Time Decay
timeDecay.description: More credit to touchpoints closer to conversion
timeDecay.difference: Recent touchpoints receive more credit. Channels closer to conversion (retargeting, branded search) are favored, but early touches still receive some credit.

positionBased.name: Position-Based
positionBased.description: 40% first, 40% last, 20% split across middle touchpoints
positionBased.difference: First and last touchpoints receive 40% each, middle touches share 20%. Values both discovery and closing channels.

dataDriven.name: Data-Driven
dataDriven.description: ML-weighted credits based on historical conversion patterns
dataDriven.difference: ML-weighted credits based on historical conversion patterns. Credits shift based on which touchpoints statistically drive the most conversions.

viewThrough.name: View-Through
viewThrough.description: Credits impressions within a configurable view-through window (1-7d)
viewThrough.difference: Credits ad impressions that occur within a configurable view-through window before conversion. Surfaces the role of brand awareness and non-click exposures.

probabilistic.name: Probabilistic
probabilistic.description: Statistical attribution for cross-device and cookie-blocked conversions
probabilistic.difference: Uses statistical modeling to attribute conversions across devices and environments where cookies are blocked. Complements deterministic click-based models.

banner.title: Unlock the Full Picture of Your Ad Performance
banner.body: Most advertisers waste 20-40% of their budget on channels that get false credit. Enhanced attribution connects your store, email, ads, and analytics into one unified view — so you can see exactly which touchpoints drive real revenue, not just clicks.
banner.dedupBody: Stop double-counting conversions across your ad platforms
banner.roasBody: Know your real return on every dollar, not inflated platform numbers
banner.budgetBody: Move spend to the channels that actually drive purchases

integrationsTab.title: Your Integration Hub
integrationsTab.description: This is where you can manage all your connected data sources. The more you connect, the more accurate your attribution becomes. You already set some up during onboarding — you can always add more here.

attributionComparison.title: Platform vs Adcero Attribution
attributionComparison.description: Platforms self-report inflated numbers because they each claim the same conversion. This card shows what Adcero actually attributes after deduplication — the real numbers are almost always lower.

incrementality.title: What is incrementality testing?
incrementality.body: Are your ads actually working, or would those customers have bought anyway? Incrementality helps you find out. It works by temporarily turning off ads for a small group and comparing their behavior to people who still see ads. If the group seeing ads converts more, you know the ads are driving real results — not just taking credit for sales that would have happened on their own.

budget.title: What is budget planning?
budget.body: Should you spend more on Meta or Google? Budget planning answers that by looking at where your money works hardest. It spots when a channel is maxed out — where spending more barely moves the needle — and suggests moving that budget to channels where it will have a bigger impact. Same total budget, better results.

comparison.windowsHelp: Meta reports conversions across multiple attribution windows. Click-through (7d) counts purchases within 7 days of clicking an ad. View-through (1d) counts purchases within 1 day of viewing an ad without clicking. Engaged-view (1d) counts purchases within 1 day of watching a video ad for a qualifying duration. These windows can overlap — the total shown is Meta's deduplicated count.
comparison.viewThroughDisclaimer: View-through and engaged-view counts are reported by Meta and cannot be independently verified at the order level.

explainability.title: Channel Attribution Weights
explainability.howItWorksBody1: Attribution weights show how much credit each marketing channel receives for driving conversions. The data-driven model uses Shapley values to fairly distribute credit based on each channel's marginal contribution.
explainability.howItWorksBody2: A channel with a higher weight means it had a greater impact on conversions during this period. The delta shows how much the weight changed compared to the previous period, measured in percentage points (pp).

jobs.unaware: Name the problem before you name the product. Nothing about your brand lands until the cost of the status quo does.
jobs.problemAware: Show that a fix exists and that it looks like your category. You are selling the solution shape, not the label on it.
jobs.solutionAware: Say what makes your version different: the mechanism, not the promise. Everyone in the category is already promising the outcome.
jobs.productAware: Close the gap between wanting it and buying it: proof, comparisons, guarantees, the price framed against what it replaces.
jobs.mostAware: Just make the offer. A deadline, a bundle, a restock: anything that beats "later".

framework.title: The Five Stages of Customer Awareness
framework.source: The framework this chapter is built on: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (1966).
framework.intro: A buyer is never simply in or out of the market. They sit somewhere on a five-step path that runs from not knowing they have a problem to waiting for a reason to buy today. Where they sit decides what the ad has to say: the message that closes someone at the end of the path is noise to someone at the start, and the message that wakes someone at the start bores everyone who already knows you.
framework.why: Every persona in this chapter comes out of your own distilled customer voice, and the stage is the only ordinal thing we know about one, so the chapter hangs off it as a ladder rather than a grid. The ordering is the insight. A rung with nobody on it isn't a missing card; it's an audience your evidence hasn't reached yet, and usually an ad you haven't written.

method.kept: Kept mentions are the customer posts, reviews and comments that passed relevance filtering during brand listening. Everything in the customer chapters is distilled from them; a mention that was filtered out contributes to nothing in this book.
method.themes: Themes are ranked by recency-decayed frequency, so a mention from this month counts for more than one from last year. Quotes are printed verbatim and were mechanically verified as substrings of their source text when the fact was written — none of them is paraphrased, summarised or generated.
method.market: Market patterns are measured as replication weight over winner-gated competitor ads: how often an approach reappears across ads that ran long enough to count as winners. Shares are computed against their own dimension total, so the shares within one dimension sum to 100%.

model.landscapeMethod: The competitive landscape sets up to {maxCompetitors} competitor profiles listened to in Brand Presence beside this brand, one sheet each, most-mentioned first. Kept mentions are counted per profile and per platform. The sentiment mix weights each scored customer theme by its frequency, and two mixes are compared only when both sides carry a scored theme weight of at least {minSample}; a gap under {levelBand} points reads as level. Themes are the most frequent per kind. Quotes are printed verbatim, ranked, and only in the merchant's language; one longer than {quoteChars} characters is cut at a word boundary and marked "…".
model.performanceMethod: What's working for you sums your own labeled ads' platform-reported spend, purchases and purchase value per creative label over the window shown, converted to one currency account by account before anything is added. Shares are a value's spend divided by its dimension's spend, so they sum to 100%. Returns (purchase value ÷ spend) and cost per purchase are stated only once a value has at least {minPurchases} purchases. Own ads carry no brand, so an organization with several brands reads one pooled set.

tooltip.title: Win score (0–100)
tooltip.intro: Ad Library has no spend data, so the score proxies how much a brand is winning with an ad. It blends three signals:
tooltip.longevity: Longevity - how long the ad has run (maxes out at 120 days)
tooltip.replication: Replication - how many ads the brand runs in that same angle (each doubling counts the same; maxes out at 128 variants)
tooltip.reach: EU reach - where Meta reports it (maxes out at 1M people reached)

economics.contributionMarginHint: Revenue left after ALL variable costs (COGS, shipping, fulfillment, fees, returns) — before ad spend. Not gross margin.
economics.aovHint: New-customer / acquisition order value. Bridges CPA ↔ ROAS.
economics.aovHintFirstOrder: Median first order, last 90 days ({orders, number} orders).
economics.aovHintOrder: Median order, last 90 days ({orders, number} orders).
economics.cacHint: Hard acquisition guardrail — the most you'll pay for one new customer.
economics.targetRoasHint: The "good (not just breakeven)" bar that drives when to scale, measured on {basis}.
economics.targetCplHint: The most a qualified lead may cost. Nothing derives this — only you know it.
economics.leadValueHint: Close rate × customer value. Profit per lead = lead value − target CPL.
economics.calculatorIntro: Build contribution margin from your cost stack. Used only when Contribution margin above is left blank — a directly entered margin always wins.
economics.cogsHint: Landed cost of goods as a % of revenue. COGS alone yields gross (optimistic) margin.
economics.paymentFeesHint: Processor + gateway fees as a % of revenue.
economics.returnsReserveHint: Return rate × net loss per return, as a % of revenue.
economics.shippingSubsidyHint: Shipping cost you absorb per order. Needs AOV to convert to a margin %.
economics.fulfillmentHint: Pick / pack / 3PL handling per order. Needs AOV to convert to a margin %.
economics.optimisticNote: (optimistic — per-order $ costs need AOV, or only COGS provided)
economics.marginSetDirectly: Contribution margin is set directly above, so this cost stack is informational only.
economics.targetCpaHint: Campaign cost-per-acquisition target. Defaults to the first-order CAC ceiling.
economics.maxCacHint: Hard acquisition guardrail — the most you'll pay per customer.
economics.minRoasHintWithBasis: The floor below which a campaign is cut, measured on {basis}. Defaults to breakeven (1 / margin).
economics.minRoasHint: The floor below which a campaign is cut. Defaults to breakeven (1 / margin).
economics.targetProfitHint: Desired contribution above breakeven. Derives target ROAS = (1 + this) / margin when Target ROAS is blank.

derived.targetRoasUnset: set a target or profit goal

warnings.targetRoasBelowBreakeven: Target ROAS {target} is below breakeven {breakeven} (1 / contribution margin). A target under breakeven loses money on every order unless it is an LTV-funded loss leader.
warnings.minRoasBelowBreakeven: Minimum-acceptable ROAS {min} is below breakeven {breakeven}; campaigns at that floor lose money.
warnings.minRoasAboveTarget: Minimum-acceptable ROAS {min} should be ≤ target ROAS {target}.
warnings.targetCplAboveLeadValue: Target CPL {targetCpl} exceeds lead value {leadValue} — every lead loses money at that target.
warnings.roasTierMismatch: Target ROAS uses the {targetTier} tier but minimum-acceptable ROAS uses {minTier}; comparing them mixes measurement tiers.

ruleCopy.gDisapprovedAd: "{label}" is disapproved and not serving. Reason: {reason}. Fix the flagged policy issue or replace the ad to restore delivery.
ruleCopy.gPmaxAdStrength: Performance Max asset group "{name}" has {strength} ad strength on {date} ({impressions} impressions). Add or improve headlines, descriptions, and assets to lift ad strength.
ruleCopy.gRankLost: Campaign "{name}" lost {share} of impressions to ad rank over {days} days.
ruleCopy.gRankLostDominant: The dominant weakness is {component} ({count} of {total} keywords below average).
ruleCopy.gRankLostNoComponent: No keyword-level Quality Score components are below average on record — the rank loss is likely a bid/competitiveness issue rather than Quality Score.
ruleCopy.gLowRatedAssetText: The {field} "{text}" is rated LOW by Google over {days} days with {impressions} impressions. Replace it with a stronger variant to lift ad strength.
ruleCopy.gLowRatedAssetId: The {field} {fieldCode} asset {assetId} is rated LOW by Google over {days} days with {impressions} impressions. Replace it with a stronger variant to lift ad strength.
ruleCopy.gMatchTypeOverlap: The keyword "{keyword}" is active under {count} match types ({matchTypes}), so a single query can match more than one — muddying bid control and spend attribution. Consolidate to the tightest match type that still covers the intent.
ruleCopy.gDuplicateKeyword: The keyword "{keyword}" ({matchType}) is active in {count} ad groups, so they compete against each other in the auction. Consolidate to one ad group to avoid cannibalization.
ruleCopy.gWastedTermAdGroup: The search term "{term}" spent {spend} on {clicks} clicks over {days} days with 0 conversions. Adding it as a ad group-level negative ({matchType}) stops the wasted spend, projected {monthly}/month.
ruleCopy.gWastedTermCampaign: The search term "{term}" spent {spend} on {clicks} clicks over {days} days with 0 conversions. Adding it as a campaign-level negative ({matchType}) stops the wasted spend, projected {monthly}/month.
ruleCopy.gHighCpaTerm: The converting term "{term}" has a CPA of {cpa} over {days} days — more than {multiple}× your max acceptable CAC of {maxCac}. It still converts, so review it manually before excluding.
ruleCopy.gBudgetCappedRaise: Campaign "{name}" lost {share} of impressions to budget over {days} days while converting ({conversions} conversions). Raising the daily budget from {current} to {raised} (+{step}) lets it capture more of the converting demand it is currently missing.
ruleCopy.gBudgetCappedReview: Campaign "{name}" lost {share} of impressions to budget over {days} days while converting ({conversions} conversions). Its current daily budget is not on record, so review and raise it manually to capture more of that converting demand.
ruleCopy.gBelowBreakevenFact: Campaign "{name}" ran at {roas} ROAS over {days} days ({spend} spend, {value} value) — below the {line} breakeven line.
ruleCopy.gBelowBreakevenLower: Lower the daily budget from {current} to {lowered} (−{step}).
ruleCopy.gBelowBreakevenReview: Its current daily budget is not on record, so review and lower it manually.
ruleCopy.gReallocCandidates: Frees ~{freed}/month; campaigns losing budget IS above breakeven: {names}.
ruleCopy.gKeywordExpansion: The search term "{term}" converted {conversions} times ({value} value) over {days} days but is not yet a keyword. Adding it as an EXACT keyword in this ad group gives it its own bid and match control (broad already delivers it, so this is a control move, not new spend).
ruleCopy.gTargetCpaLower: Campaign "{name}" ran at {cpa} CPA over the window ({conversions} conversions), above your {maxCac} max CAC, while its target CPA is set at {current}. Lower the target CPA to {proposed} to steer bids toward profitable acquisitions.
ruleCopy.gTargetRoasLower: Campaign "{name}" ran at {roas} ROAS — well above its {target} target and the {breakeven} breakeven line — with headroom to win more impressions. Lower the target ROAS to {proposed} (still ≥ breakeven) so bids reach for the volume you're leaving on the table.
ruleCopy.gTargetRoasRaise: Campaign "{name}" has a target ROAS of {target} — below the {breakeven} breakeven line — and is delivering {roas} ROAS, losing money on every order. Raise the target ROAS to {proposed} to pull bids back toward profitability.
ruleCopy.mRejectedAd: "{label}" is rejected inside a live ad set, so it is not delivering. Reason: {detail}. Fix the flagged policy issue or replace the creative to restore delivery.
ruleCopy.mFlaggedAd: "{label}" is flagged with policy issues inside a live ad set, so it is not delivering. Reason: {detail}. Fix the flagged policy issue or replace the creative to restore delivery.
ruleCopy.mNewCustomerCac: "{label}" paid {nCac} per NEW customer on {spend} of spend ({newCustomers} new of {known} first-party purchases with a known customer type, {newPct} new) — above the {ceiling} ceiling. A retargeting or repeat-purchase ad set can legitimately look like this, so review before changing budget — no mutation is proposed.
ruleCopy.mNewCustomerCacBlended: "{label}" paid {nCac} per NEW customer on {spend} of spend ({newCustomers} new of {known} first-party purchases with a known customer type, {newPct} new) — above the {ceiling} ceiling, while its blended cost per purchase was {blended}. A retargeting or repeat-purchase ad set can legitimately look like this, so review before changing budget — no mutation is proposed.
ruleCopy.mZeroDelivery: "{label}" spent nothing in the last {days} days after averaging {priorDaily}/day over the previous {priorDays}, while still active on a {budget}/day budget. Check for a rejected creative, an exhausted audience, an ended schedule, or a billing hold.
ruleCopy.mUnderPacing: "{label}" spent an average of {mean}/day over the last {days} days against a {budget}/day budget ({utilization} utilization). Narrow targeting, a low bid, or limited creative can all starve delivery — review before adding budget it is not using.
ruleCopy.mCplStall: "{label}" spent {spend} over {days} spending days and produced no leads at all (target cost per lead {target}).
ruleCopy.mCplAbove: "{label}" paid {cpl} per lead on {spend} of spend ({leads} leads) — more than {multiple}× the {target} target.
ruleCopy.mCplNoOwnBudget: This ad set has no daily budget of its own, so lower it at the campaign level or rework the targeting.
ruleCopy.mCplNoOwnBudgetCampaign: This ad set has no daily budget of its own (its campaign runs on {campaignBudget}/day), so lower it at the campaign level or rework the targeting.
ruleCopy.mCplAtFloor: Its daily budget ({current}) is already at the minimum {floor}, so pause it or rework the offer instead of lowering.
ruleCopy.mLowerBudget: Lower the daily budget from {current} to {lowered} (−{step}), freeing about {freed}/month to reallocate.
ruleCopy.mBreakevenFact: "{label}" returned {roas} on {spend} of spend over {days} spending days ({basis} basis) — below the {line} line.
ruleCopy.mBreakevenRulersDisagree: The {other} ruler reads {roas}, at or above the line, so the two measurements disagree. Review before cutting — no budget change is proposed.
ruleCopy.mBreakevenNoOwnBudget: This ad set has no daily budget of its own, so lower it at the campaign level or exclude this ad set.
ruleCopy.mBreakevenNoOwnBudgetCampaign: This ad set has no daily budget of its own (its campaign runs on {campaignBudget}/day), so lower it at the campaign level or exclude this ad set.
ruleCopy.mBreakevenAtFloor: Its daily budget ({current}) is already at the minimum {floor}, so pause or restructure it instead of lowering.
ruleCopy.mScaleFact: "{label}" returned {roas} on {spend} of spend with {purchases} purchases ({basis} basis) — at least {multiple}× the {target} target.
ruleCopy.mScaleRulersDisagree: The {other} ruler reads {roas}, below the {breakeven} breakeven, so the two measurements disagree. Review before scaling — no budget change is proposed.
ruleCopy.mScaleNoOwnBudget: This ad set has no daily budget of its own, so scale it at the campaign level.
ruleCopy.mScaleNoOwnBudgetCampaign: This ad set has no daily budget of its own (its campaign runs on {campaignBudget}/day), so scale it at the campaign level.
ruleCopy.mScaleRaise: It is already spending {mean}/day against a {current}/day budget ({utilization} utilization). Raise the daily budget to {raised} (+{step}). No dollar projection is claimed — added budget is not guaranteed to hold this return.
ruleCopy.mCreativeFatigue: "{label}" lost {decline} of its click-through rate over the window ({prior} → {recent}, z = {z}) while still spending {spend} in the recent half. Refresh the creative — the audience has seen it.
ruleCopy.mLaneFatigue: "{label}" now costs {recent} per conversion over the last 7 days, {ratio}× the {early} it cost in its first 14 days of delivery in this window. Refresh the creative — the audience has seen it.
ruleCopy.mZeroConversionAd: "{label}" has spent {spend} in this window with {conversions, plural, =0 {no conversions} one {# conversion} other {# conversions}} — {spendCpa}× the ad set's cost per conversion of {cpa}, at or past the {limitCpa}× safety limit for its conversion count. Consider pausing it in Meta Ads Manager and replacing it with a fresh creative.
ruleCopy.kNegativeAdGroup: Proposed from Keyword Research: exclude "{keyword}" ({match}) so it stops matching your ads in this ad group.
ruleCopy.kNegativeCampaign: Proposed from Keyword Research: exclude "{keyword}" ({match}) so it stops matching your ads in this campaign.
ruleCopy.kKeyword: Proposed from Keyword Research: target "{keyword}" ({match}) as a new keyword in this ad group.
ruleCopy.alPromoteConcept: "{concept}" has brought {conversions, plural, one {# result} other {# results}} at {cpa} each — a {probability} chance it beats the rest of the ad set. Keep it running and consider giving it more budget in Meta Ads Manager.
ruleCopy.alRetireConcept: "{concept}" lost {rounds, plural, one {# fair round} other {# fair rounds}} against the rest of the ad set using {ads, plural, one {# ad} other {# different ads}}. Pause its ads in Meta Ads Manager. Adcero has stopped testing this idea in this ad set.
ruleCopy.alAddConceptAds: "{concept}" lost {rounds, plural, one {# round} other {# rounds}} against the rest of the ad set, but {ads, plural, =0 {none of its ads} one {only # of its ads} other {only # of its ads}} got delivery — Adcero needs at least {minAds, plural, one {# ad} other {# ads}} with delivery before it can judge the idea. Consider adding new ads for it in Meta Ads Manager.
ruleCopy.alReplaceStarvedAds: Meta has barely shown the ads for "{concept}" in the last {days, plural, one {day} other {# days}}, while the rest of the ad set spent normally. Consider publishing a fresh batch of ads for this concept in Meta Ads Manager (replacement batch {retry, number}).
ruleCopy.alShelveConcept: Meta barely showed "{concept}" after {batches, plural, one {# batch} other {# batches}} of new ads ({ads, plural, one {# ad} other {# ads}} in total). Pause its ads in Meta Ads Manager; the idea can be tried again after {until}.
ruleCopy.alPauseAd: "{ad}" spent {spend} with {conversions, plural, =0 {no results} one {# result} other {# results}} — {spendCpa}× your usual cost per result ({cpa}). Consider pausing it in Meta Ads Manager.
ruleCopy.alRefreshAd: "{ad}" now costs {recent} per result over the last 7 days — {ratio}× the {early} it cost in its first 14 days. Consider making a fresh version of the same concept and swapping it in for this ad in Meta Ads Manager.
ruleCopy.alNoEvidence: Adcero suggests this from your recent results in this ad set. Nothing changes until you act in Meta Ads Manager.

start.metaDescription: Your free Meta Ad Account Health Check from the Adcero ChatGPT app.

reports.previewUnavailable: This report’s preview is not available.

privacy.metaDescription: How the Adcero ChatGPT plugin handles the data you share with it.
privacy.title: Adcero ChatGPT plugin — privacy

receives.heading: What the plugin receives
receives.body: When you run the Ad Account Health Check in ChatGPT, the plugin receives your Meta Ads Manager export (CSV): either the file you attach, which it downloads once from ChatGPT's temporary download link, or the text you paste. It also receives an optional break-even target if you give one. It does not receive your ad account login, and it never connects to or changes your ad account.

stores.heading: What we store
stores.body: We store only the derived report: the summary numbers, the score, the findings, and the checks we could not run. The file itself is never stored — it is processed in memory and discarded. We do not assign you a visitor id, and the report is not tied to your name or email.

ipAddress.heading: Your IP address
ipAddress.body: To prevent abuse, the plugin limits how many checks can be run from one network. It uses your IP address for this in memory only: the address is not stored, not logged with report data, and not shared.

retention.heading: How long we keep it
retention.body: An unclaimed report is deleted 14 days after it was created. If you sign up and claim the report into your Adcero workspace, it is kept as part of that workspace until you delete the workspace.

access.heading: Who can see it
access.body: Anyone holding the report link can view it until it expires — the link contains a long random token, so treat it like a password. Once claimed, the report is visible to members of the workspace that claimed it.

noSale.heading: No sale of data
noSale.body: We do not sell your data, and we do not use your export or your report to advertise to you or to anyone else.

policies.heading: Other policies
policies.body: This page covers the ChatGPT plugin. Adcero's <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> and <terms>Terms of Service</terms> apply to everything else, including an Adcero account if you create one.

support.metaDescription: Get help with the Adcero Ad Account Health Check plugin for ChatGPT.
support.title: Ad Account Health Check support
support.description: Help with the Adcero plugin in ChatGPT.

contact.heading: Contact us
contact.body: Email <email>{address}</email> with the date you ran the check and what you expected to see. Please don't send your ad export unless we ask for it.

export.heading: Getting the right export
export.body: In Meta Ads Manager, open the Ads tab, set the date range to the last 30 days, choose Breakdown > By time > Day, then export the table as a CSV and attach it in ChatGPT. The check needs at least 7 days of data.

errors.heading: If the check can't run
errors.body: The plugin tells you why: a missing column, too few days, or a file that isn't a Meta Ads Manager export. Export again with the steps above and retry.

data.heading: Your data
data.body: The plugin never connects to or changes your ad account. Read <privacy>how the ChatGPT app handles your data</privacy>.

descriptions.mostPostEngagement: We'll try to get the most likes, comments, shares, or other engagement on your post.
descriptions.mostEventResponses: We'll try to get the most responses for your event.

descriptions.asManyTimes: We'll try to show your ads to people as many times as possible.

descriptions.conversationInstagram: We'll try to show your ads to people most likely to start a conversation with you through Instagram.
descriptions.conversationMessenger: We'll try to show your ads to people most likely to start a conversation with you through Messenger.
descriptions.oncePerDay: We'll try to show your ads to people up to once per day.
descriptions.rememberAds: We'll try to show your ads to people who are likely to remember seeing them.
descriptions.installApp: We'll try to show your ads to people who are most likely to install your app.

descriptions.shareContactInfo: We'll try to show your ads to the people most likely to share their contact information with you.
descriptions.specificActionGeneric: We'll try to show your ads to the people most likely to take a specific action (e.g., submit a form, make a purchase, or start a chat).

descriptions.specificActionMessaging: We'll try to show your ads to the people most likely to take a specific action through messaging.
descriptions.viewWebsite: We'll try to show your ads to the people most likely to view the website or Instant Experience linked in your ad.
descriptions.twoSecondPlays: We'll try to show your video ads to people who are likely to watch 2 continuous seconds or more. Most 2-second continuous video plays will have at least 50% of the video pixels on screen.
descriptions.thruPlay: We'll try to show your video ads to people who will watch the entire video when it's shorter than 15 seconds. For longer videos, we'll try to show it to people who are likely to watch at least 15 seconds.

about.title: About Special Ad Categories
about.intro: Some types of ads — like those about jobs, housing, credit, politics, or social issues — have extra rules to make sure everyone gets treated fairly. Meta calls these "Special Ad Categories."
about.rules: If your ad is about one of these topics, you'll need to let us know so we can help you follow Meta's rules. These rules limit how you can target people — for example, you won't be able to target by age, gender, or ZIP code in some cases.

about.listFair: Ensures a fair experience for all users

financial.creditNote: Credit is now part of financial products and services.
financial.additionalInfo: For additional information, read <link>About ads for financial products and services</link>.
financial.infoTitle: About ads for financial products and services

about.introduced: As part of our ongoing efforts to promote fairness on our advertising platform, we have introduced a new Special Ad Category "Financial products and services" for advertisers promoting financial products and services. Starting {date}, using this category is required for financial products and services campaigns for advertisers based in the United States or showing ads to audiences in the United States. Ads may be rejected if an appropriate category is not chosen. <link>Learn more about the update here</link>.
about.discriminatoryPractices: To help prevent discrimination, our <link>Discriminatory Practices</link> advertising policy has special requirements for ads related to financial products and services.
about.creditReplaced: Note: The Credit Special Ad Category has been replaced by the Financial Products and Services category. This video covers the credit components that are in scope for our requirements. Additionally, this category has expanded to include financial products and services, which you can learn more about here.
about.whenRequired: When you run financial products and services ads, you may need to choose a Special Ad Category during the creation of your campaign. You'll need to do this if:

requirements.usAdvertiser: You're an advertiser in the United States
requirements.usAudience: Your audience is in the United States
requirements.creditRegions: You're running ads for credit opportunities in the US, Canada or certain parts of Europe or reaching audiences in these regions

regions.ukBases: UK sovereign bases in Cyprus (Akrotiri and Dhekeli)

about.mayBeRejected: If you meet the qualifications above and don't choose a Special Ad Category, your ad may be rejected.
about.adsHeading: Ads for financial products and services
about.required: Starting {date}, use of the financial products and services Special Ad Category is required for advertisers based in the United States or showing financial products and services campaigns to audiences in the United States. Ads may be rejected if the advertiser does not choose an appropriate Special Ad Category. Our policy for credit ads (a subset of financial products and services) does not change, and will continue to apply to advertisers based in the US or showing ads to audiences in the US, Canada or certain parts of Europe.
about.unsure: If you're unsure whether your ad is covered under Meta's Discriminatory Practices policy for housing, employment or financial products and services ads, you can review examples of covered ads below.
about.coveredHeading: Ads that promote or directly link to a financial product or service offer, including credit
about.examplesIntro: Here are some examples of ads for credit, a subset of financial products and services, under our policies:
about.exampleCarAlt: Example ad for Mod Electrica cars
about.includesHeading: They can include offers for the following and more in the US, Canada or certain parts of Europe:

includes.creditCardBrandAds: Brand ads for credit cards, regardless of offer
includes.loans: Loans, including auto, mortgage, personal or business loans

about.usHeading: Additionally, in the US, they can also include other financial products and services like the following and more:

us.banking: Banking services including checking and savings accounts
us.financialBrandAds: Brand ads for financial products and services, regardless of offer
us.installments: 0% APR installment payments, including buy now, pay later (BNPL) and in-house installment payments

about.excludesHeading: They don't include offers for the following:

excludes.b2b: Business-to-Business (B2B) only financial products and services

about.audienceBody: When you choose a Special Ad Category, we apply additional audience restrictions to your campaign. These restrictions are a preventative measure to protect people from discriminatory practices. Your audience options don't become limited to only people interested in financial products and services opportunities. Learn more about <link>targeting restrictions for financial products and services ads</link>.
about.chooseCategory: If you determine that your ad is for financial products and services, learn how to <link>choose a Special Ad Category in Ads Manager</link>. Remember that choosing a Special Ad Category doesn't impact how long it takes for us to review your ads.
about.troubleshoot: Learn more about how to <troubleshoot>troubleshoot a rejected ad</troubleshoot>. If you believe your ad was rejected incorrectly, you can request a review in <support>Business Support Home</support>.

traffic.intro: The traffic objective is designed to send people to a destination, like your website or app.
traffic.chooseIf: Choose the traffic objective if you want to:

reasons.website: Send people to your website or app.
reasons.conversations: Increase conversations on WhatsApp or Messenger
reasons.calls: Encourage people to call your business.
reasons.clicks: Show your ad to people most likely to click it.

traffic.example: For example, if you're having a flash sale in your shop or want to send potential customers to a web page that describes your services this may help drive traffic to those destinations.

appPromotion.intro: App promotion ads allow you to promote your app across Facebook, Instagram and Meta Audience Network. You can create ads with the app promotion objective from Meta Ads Manager.
appPromotion.register: To get the most out of your ads, you'll want to register your app with Facebook and set up an integration such as the Facebook SDK, which will enable you to pass app event data from your app to Facebook. With app event data, you can accurately track and measure the actions people take in your app.
appPromotion.noRegistration: You don't need to register your app or set up an integration in order to run ads using the app promotion objective, but your ads will automatically optimize for link clicks rather than app installs. In addition, your campaign will not track any installs that happen as a result of your ads unless your app is registered and your integration is correctly implemented.
appPromotion.createIntro: To create your ad from Ads Manager:

steps.chooseAccount: Choose the ad account associated with your app.
steps.clickCreate: Click + Create in the top left.
steps.chooseCampaignType: Choose the Manual app promotion campaign option if you wish to create standard app ads. Choose Advantage+ app campaign and follow these instructions if you wish to simplify the ad creation process. Click Continue.
steps.addDetails: Add your campaign details, iOS 14+ campaign, A/B test and Meta Advantage+ campaign budget information if needed, then click Next.
steps.chooseApp: In the App section, choose the app you want to promote.
steps.chooseAppNote: Note that if your app is not linked to your ad account, your ad will optimize for link clicks rather than app installs. You'll not be able to optimize for any app events without first linking your app to your ad account.
steps.performanceGoalAppEvents: Choose Maximize number of app events to optimize for people who are most likely to take a specific action within your app, like making a purchase.
steps.performanceGoalInstalls: Choose Maximize number of app installs to optimize for people who are most likely to download your app.
steps.performanceGoalIosNote: Note: If you're creating an iOS 14+ campaign, select your performance goal below the App promotion section at the ad set level.
steps.chooseBudget: Choose your budget, audience and placements.
steps.attribution: If you're creating an iOS 14+ campaign, choose your campaign attribution method. Learn about campaign attribution methods.
steps.identity: In the Identity section, select your Facebook Page and attach your Instagram account, if applicable.
steps.adSetup: In the Ad setup section, select Flexible, Single image or video or Carousel.
steps.adCreative: In the Ad creative section, choose the image(s) or video(s) that you would like to use for your ad.
steps.addText: Add the headline, description and other text to include in your ad. Include the call-to-action button that is most relevant to your app ad.
steps.completeAd: Complete the rest of your ad by adding information in the Languages and Tracking section, if applicable.
steps.publish: When you're done, click Publish to publish your app ad.

appPromotion.otherObjectives: You can also create an app ad using the traffic or sales objectives and entering your App ID in the Traffic or Sales section, respectively. You'll not be able to use Advantage+ app campaigns with either of these objectives.
appPromotion.results: After your ad is published and reviewed, you can see the results of your app ads from Ads Manager or by working with a mobile measurement partner.
appPromotion.iosNote: Note: There are several changes you may need to make to set up, run and manage your ad accounts, campaigns and ad sets in order to reach people using iOS 14.5 and later devices. Learn more about account and campaign considerations for setting up and managing app promotion campaigns for people who use iOS 14.5 and later devices.

abTest.title: A/B test types available on Meta technologies
abTest.intro: There are several ways to create A/B tests on Meta technologies depending on the variable you're trying to test and where you start creating your A/B test.
abTest.newToTesting: Note: New to A/B Testing? Learn more about how A/B tests work in Meta Ads Manager and the Experiments tool.
abTest.recommendToolbar: Generally, we recommend creating an A/B test with the Meta Ads Manager toolbar, which uses an existing ad campaign or ad set as a template for your test. To use this toolbar:

toolbarSteps.mainTable: Go to the Ads Manager main table. This page lists all of your available ads, campaigns and ad sets on your ad account.
toolbarSteps.checkBox: Check the box to the left of the campaign(s) or ad set(s) you want to use for an A/B test.
toolbarSteps.clickAbTest: From the toolbar above, click A/B test.
toolbarSteps.selectVariable: Select an available variable and follow the on-screen instructions.

abTest.customNote: Note: If you select Custom you can create a test by duplicating the selected campaign or ad set and edit any variables in the new test campaign.
abTest.results: All A/B tests use the same underlying technology to compare a different creative, audience or placement and determine a winner. All your test results will be available in: Experiments once the test is finished.
abTest.otherWaysHeading: Other ways you can create an A/B test

otherWays.experiments: Directly from the Experiments tool—in Experiments you can create or duplicate ad campaigns to compare and determine a winning strategy. The Experiments tool is useful when you want the flexibility of fine tuning your ad campaigns before starting your test, or when you want to use several existing ad campaigns for your test.
otherWays.newCampaign: When creating a new ad campaign—you can choose to A/B test when creating a new ad campaign. This option is useful when you want to conveniently test a variable while creating a new ad campaign. Note: because of A/B test updates, this option may not be available to you at this time.
otherWays.duplicate: By duplicating an existing campaign, ad set or ad—you can duplicate and create an A/B test in Ads Manager if you want to quickly make a change to an existing ad and compare performance:
otherWays.duplicateCampaign: Duplicating an existing campaign lets you compare by changing one or more variables to determine a winning strategy.
otherWays.duplicateAdSetOrAd: Duplicating an existing ad set or ad lets you choose a variable and we'll walk you through the kinds of changes you can make to compare and determine a winning strategy.
otherWays.prompt: From a common scenarios prompt—sometimes we'll suggest you run an A/B test to try a new business strategy or if we think your current ad might benefit from a test. These prompts will show you how to do this in a few steps from Experiments.

performanceGoal.intro: Your performance goal is the result you want to achieve from your ad. Meta's delivery system uses this goal to find the best people to show your ads to and get more of that result.
performanceGoal.example: For example, if your performance goal is to maximize the number of link clicks, we'll try to show your ad to people who are most likely to click your ad's link.

attribution.title: Attribution Settings
attribution.description: Configure how conversions are attributed to your ads
attribution.headerTooltip: This attribution setting is a finite period of time during which conversions can be credited to your ads and used to inform campaign optimization. For example, with a 35-day click setting, our system will learn from conversions that happen within 35 days and show ads to people most likely to convert within 35 days. Multiple attribution settings can be selected for reporting. You can see more details when you use Compare attribution settings in the campaign table.
attribution.standardDescription: Optimize delivery for a selected time window and interaction type. You can use the default or edit this below.
attribution.incrementalDescription: Optimize delivery for incremental conversions using sophisticated models that predict whether a conversion is caused by an ad.
attribution.clickThroughTooltip: Click-through is when someone clicks your ad and converts within the period of time that you select. We'll learn from your click-through conversions, and show your ads to people likely to click-through within the same period of time.
attribution.engagedViewTooltip: Engaged-view is when someone views your ad and takes an action within 1 day. For images, engaged-views are counted when an image is visible on at least 50% of the screen for 2 seconds. For videos, engaged-views are counted when a video is played for at least 10 seconds or for 97% of its total length if it's shorter than 10 seconds. We'll learn from your engaged-view conversions, and show your ads to people likely to engage-view within the same period of time.
attribution.engagedViewPlacements: Engaged-view is available for all placements except Facebook in-stream video ads, which cannot be skipped.
attribution.viewThroughTooltip: View-through is when someone sees your ad, doesn't click it, but still takes an action within the period of time you select. We'll learn from your view-through conversions and show your ads to people likely to convert within the same period of time.

aboutDynamicCreative.access: To keep our platform safe from harm and to prevent advertising abuse, we only grant access to some features when an advertiser has met certain requirements. This means when you create a new business portfolio or ad account, you may not have access to all advertising features. You can see what features you currently have access to, and find out what actions you may need to take to access additional features in <link>Business Support Home</link>.
aboutDynamicCreative.intro: Dynamic creative takes multiple media, such as images and videos, and multiple ad components, such as images, videos, text, audio and calls-to-action, and then mixes and matches them in new ways to improve your ad performance. It allows you to automatically create personalized creative variations for each person who views your ad, with results that are scalable.
aboutDynamicCreative.noteSalesApp: As of June 2024, you may no longer be able to use dynamic creative when creating ad sets on Ads Manager when you select sales or app promotion as your objective. While existing campaigns leveraging dynamic creative will be unaffected at this time, using flexible ad format to achieve a similar result is recommended. Learn more about the flexible ad format.
aboutDynamicCreative.noteUnsupported: Dynamic creative doesn't work with <languagesLink>ads in multiple languages</languagesLink> or asset customization or <politicalLink>ads with political content</politicalLink>.
aboutDynamicCreative.optimizeIntro: The creative variations are only based on the media and ad components you provide unless the Optimize creative for each person toggle is also turned on. When that toggle is also enabled, the following optimizations might occur:
aboutDynamicCreative.enhancements: Applying minor image enhancements to thumbnails or images.

advantageAudience.title: Advantage+ Audience
advantageAudience.aiFindsAudiences: Meta's AI finds audiences for your ads.
advantageAudience.suggestionDescription: Meta's AI finds audiences for your ads. If you add an audience suggestion, you'll guide Meta's AI towards people you think are likely to respond.
advantageAudience.manualDescription: Define your audience by setting age, location, language, interests, and other criteria. Ads will only be shown to the people you specify, with no automatic expansion.
advantageAudience.manualWarning: ⚠️ Note: Meta recommends using Advantage+ targeting for better performance through broader reach and delivery optimization. Manual targeting may limit ad delivery and increase costs.
advantageAudience.specialCategories: Special Ads Category campaigns that fall within the scope of our Housing, Employment, and Financial products and services policy, Social Issues, Elections, and Politics ads and Pharmaceuticals may not have access to all Advantage+ features.
advantageAudience.renamed: Advantage+ sales campaigns is the new name for Advantage+ shopping campaigns.
advantageAudience.getTheMost: Create a campaign using Meta Advantage+ audience to get the most out of Meta's advanced AI when finding your audience.
advantageAudience.betterResults: Advantage+ audience typically gets better results compared with the original audience options. This is because our AI is not limited to delivering ads to people that match your selections, giving it more flexibility to find new audiences.
advantageAudience.createIntro: To create a campaign using Advantage+ audience:
advantageAudience.stepAdSetLevel: Create a campaign and go to the Ad set level.
advantageAudience.stepNewCampaigns: For new campaigns, Advantage+ audience is automatically applied if it's available. To turn it off, select Switch to original audience options or Further limit the reach of your ads.
advantageAudience.stepEditing: If you're editing or duplicating a campaign, select Switch to Advantage+ audience under Audience. If you duplicate a campaign with recommended settings, Advantage+ audience will be automatically applied unless you're using the Sales objective.
advantageAudience.stepSavedAudience: (Optional) Select Use saved audience under Audience controls. Settings from the saved audience you select in the search bar will be applied as either audience controls or a suggestion.
advantageAudience.stepControls: Use Audience controls to limit who can see your ads. Hover over Locations and select Edit. We recommend targeting as broadly as possible. We won't target beyond these locations unless you select Reach more people likely to respond to your ads.
advantageAudience.stepMoreOptions: (Optional) Under Audience controls, select Show more options to use:
advantageAudience.optionExclude: Exclude these custom audiences: For example, to exclude current customers. Custom audiences you exclude can still be added as Audience suggestions, such as in a prospecting campaign. It's not possible to exclude lookalike audiences.
advantageAudience.optionMinimumAge: Minimum age: For example, if your goods or services can't legally be purchased by people under 21.
advantageAudience.optionLanguages: Languages: For example, if there are languages you choose to include.
advantageAudience.stepSuggestion: (Optional) Add information about the people you want to reach as an Audience suggestion. We'll show ads to people matching your suggestion, and other audiences when it's likely to improve performance. Learn about audience suggestions.
advantageAudience.addAge: Age (if you set a Minimum age in Audience controls, it can't be overruled)
advantageAudience.limitWhereShown: If there are audiences that shouldn't see your ads, you can update your Audience controls or use Ad account settings to limit where ads are shown.
advantageAudience.limitFromAccount: If there are audiences that shouldn't see ads from your account, you can update your Audience controls or use Ad account settings to limit where ads are shown.
advantageAudience.created: You've created a campaign using Advantage+ audience. Complete your other settings before you publish your ad.
advantageAudience.aiIntro: Meta Advantage+ audience lets you use Meta's advanced AI to find your campaign audience. It can be the easiest to use and best performing Advantage+ audience automation option yet.
advantageAudience.resultAwareness: the Awareness objective could get 14.8% lower cost per result.
advantageAudience.resultTraffic: the Traffic, Engagement and Leads objectives could get 9.7% lower cost per result.
advantageAudience.resultSales: the Sales and App promotion objectives could get 7.2% lower cost per result.
advantageAudience.howItWorksIntro: Meta's AI uses numerous pieces of information to find your audience, evolving constantly as it learns. For example:
advantageAudience.autoShow: With Advantage+ audience we'll automatically show ads to people most likely to respond.
advantageAudience.suggestionsBody: Meta's AI will find your audience or add information about the people you want to reach as an Audience suggestion. We'll show ads to people matching your suggestion, and other audiences when it's likely to improve performance.
advantageAudience.whenRecommend: We recommend experimenting with Advantage+ audience for almost all campaign types, except remarketing campaigns.
advantageAudience.whenSalesApp: For campaigns using the sales or app promotion objectives, we recommend our more complete campaign solutions Advantage+ sales campaigns and Advantage+ app campaigns which apply AI across many steps. If you want to explore using AI to find your audience while still sharing knowledge about your customers but don't want to automate all steps in your campaign, Advantage+ audience is an effective alternative.
advantageAudience.abTest: Use A/B testing to compare the performance of Advantage+ audience against other audience selections. This is the only reliable way to compare 2 audience set ups.
advantageAudience.ageLimits: You can't select ages under 18 globally, 20 in Thailand and 21 in Indonesia when using Advantage+ audience.
